subject: Estimating errors in predictive accuracy using K-fold cross validation

messages.author: b17f4d0880547804
messages.subject: Estimating errors in predictive accuracy using K-fold cross validation
parts:
Hi all,
I've built a stan model used k-fold cross validation as done in Aki's paper. The only difference from the paper is that I've monitored the sum of the log likelihoods as opposed to the individual log likelihoods. I did this because of memory issues as I'm dealing with a large dataset. 

In my case, the point of doing cross validation was to compare predictive accuracy between a suite of models and ultimately choose a single 'best' model. I was hoping to do this using the mean and credible intervals of the monitored log likelihoods pooled across kfolds.

Specifically I'd:
Pool the samples of the sum log likelihood across all K-fold fits and then estimate the mean and the lower and upper 95% quantiles. My thinking was that this would capture the full uncertainty associated with estimating the log likelihood of the heldout data and allow people to determine whether there was a significant difference between model predictive accuracy. 

However, I'm beginning to think my approach isn't technically correct. Reading Aki's paper again I see that the standard error is estimated as: SQRT(N) x SD(log likelihoods).

Another approach I've seen people use is a point estimate approach whereby they extract the mean log likelihood for each kfold and then use these values to estimate the average log likelihood and confidence interval (i.e. across kfolds).

Does anyone have any guidance on how I should best approach this?

messages.author: b17f4d0880547804
messages.subject: Re: Estimating errors in predictive accuracy using K-fold cross validation
parts: I guess I should have also stated that I could use a log likelihood ratio between two models (i.e. LL of complex model/ LL of Simpler model) and compare the it to the chi-square distribution... But again I feel like this approach doesn't take into consideration the uncertainty in the estimates as it relies on a point estimate.

messages.author: a236d3d356ca53fd
messages.subject: Re: Estimating errors in predictive accuracy using K-fold cross validation
parts:
Hi,

If you need save memory, in K-fold-CV you can do like this
generated quantities {
  real log_likt;
  log_likt <- 0;
  for (n in 1:Nt)
    log_likt <- log_likt + bernoulli_logit_log(yt[n], beta0 + xt[n]*beta);
}
Then outside of Stan compute log of the expected summed densities (summing was made in Stan)
 elpdhats(k)=log(mean(exp(log_likt)) 
Then you will have K elpdhats values, instead of N values as in the paper you mention.You can then compute
standard error and pairwise model comparison using these values and K, instead of elpdhat_i and LOO as in the paper.
This approach is mentioned, e.g., in http://becs.aalto.fi/en/research/bayes/publications/VehtariLampinen_NC2002_preprint.pdf

Aki

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Re: Estimating errors in predictive accuracy using K-fold cross validation
parts:
I'm surprised this was Aki's recommendation since he's the one
who suggested I calculate it more stably using log_sum_exp:

elpdhats[k] <- log(mean(exp(log_likt)));

should be:

elpdhats[k] <- log_sum_exp(log_likt) - log(N);

where N is the number of elements in log_likt and log_sum_exp is
the usual robust implementation as

log_sum_exp(u) = max(u) + log(sum(exp(u - max(u)))

which won't underflow.

- Bob

I just went through this while writing a tutorial :-)

The problem is that log doesn't distribute through integrals
or sums; it's easy to see in the sum case for a vector x of
positive values:

mean(log(x)) != log(mean(x))
